riskFlags.title: High type 2 diabetes risk

riskFlags.title: Waist 101 cm
riskFlags.detail: Fat stored around the abdomen is closely linked to heart disease and insulin resistance.

riskFlags.title: Frequent alcohol use
riskFlags.detail: Australian guidelines recommend no more than 10 standard drinks a week and no more than 4 on any one day.

riskFlags.title: BMI 29: Overweight

riskFlags.title: High stress

recommendations.title: Book a blood glucose check with your GP
recommendations.rationale: Early detection of pre-diabetes means it can often be reversed with lifestyle change.
actions: Ask your GP for a fasting glucose or HbA1c test
Take this assessment summary to the appointment

recommendations.title: Work towards a healthier weight
recommendations.rationale: Losing even 5 to 10% of your body weight (5 to 9 kg) brings measurable health benefits.
actions: Aim for about 1990 kcal a day
Fill half your plate with vegetables at lunch and dinner
Swap sugary drinks for water or sparkling water

recommendations.title: Build up to 150 active minutes a week
recommendations.rationale: Regular movement improves insulin sensitivity, mood and sleep, independent of weight loss.
actions: Start with 3 gym sessions a week mixing cardio and strength
Include strength work twice a week

recommendations.title: Improve the quality of your meals
recommendations.rationale: A diet rich in vegetables, whole grains and lean protein supports your 30 g daily fibre target.
actions: Add a serve of vegetables to every main meal (target 5 serves a day)
Limit takeaway and fried food to once a week
Plan snacks: fruit, yoghurt or a handful of nuts

recommendations.title: Protect your sleep and manage stress
recommendations.rationale: Poor sleep and high stress raise hunger hormones and cravings for high-calorie food.
actions: Keep a consistent sleep and wake time
Try 10 minutes of walking or breathing exercises daily

recommendations.title: Cut back on alcohol
recommendations.rationale: Alcohol adds energy without nutrition and affects sleep and liver health.
actions: Have at least two alcohol-free days a week

recommendations.title: Drink about 3.2 L of water a day
recommendations.rationale: Good hydration supports concentration, digestion and appetite control.
actions: Keep a refillable bottle with you
Have a glass of water with every meal
Track intake with the NutriHelp water tracker

narrative.headline: A solid start with clear areas to improve
narrative.summary: Your overall wellness score is 56 out of 100. Your strongest area is body composition (70), while metabolic health (35) offers the biggest opportunity. Start with this: book a blood glucose check with your gp.
narrative.motivation: Small, consistent changes add up. Reassess in 4 to 6 weeks to see your progress.

disclaimer: This assessment is a wellbeing screening tool, not a medical diagnosis. Talk to your GP or an accredited practising dietitian before making major changes, especially if you have a health condition.
